maximum_permitted_stay: Up to 30 days by law; portal states 40-day permit validity; distinction unconfirmed.
passport_validity_rule: Passport valid for the entire permit duration plus at least four additional weeks.
blank_passport_pages_rule: No minimum blank-page count is published in GSGSSI visitor-permit guidance.
return_ticket_rule: No air return-ticket rule is published; vessel name and intended first arrival/departure dates are required. Access is by sea only.
proof_of_funds_rule: No separate minimum funds amount is published; the visitor permit fee and adequate health insurance are required.
accommodation_rule: No visitor accommodation ashore; visitors arrive by sea and require vessel-based support throughout the visit.
travel_insurance_rule: Adequate health insurance must cover emergency evacuation to a country with suitable treatment, transport and medical care in transit, and repatriation of remains.
yellow_fever_or_health_rule: The visitor-permit guidance does not list a vaccination requirement; adequate health insurance is mandatory. There are no medical facilities for visitors.
transit_rule: Accessible only by sea. Vessel manifests must be validated and submitted at least 72 hours before arrival. Separate visas may be needed for the embarkation or transit country.
application_channel: ETA portal https://eta.entry.gov.gs (Chrome/Edge); individual or group via authorised agent, cruise/yacht operator or family. Check if operator applies.
processing_time: No SLA published; apply at least 14 days before arrival; late and 3-day cutoffs apply.
required_documents: Ordinary passport valid for the full permit duration plus at least four additional weeks|Applicant name, date of birth and nationality matching the travel document|Valid email address for permit correspondence|Contact telephone number (recommended)|Adequate health insurance covering emergency evacuation, transport and medical care in transit, and repatriation of remains|Vessel name and intended first arrival and departure dates|Payment of the visitor permit fee|Applicant consent and contact details if a family member, travel agent or cruise/yacht operator submits the application

review_notes: PENDING — The Entry Control Ordinance 2022 section 7(3) limits a visitor permit's specified period to no more than 30 days from the expected first entry; section 7(4) permits an extension of up to 30 days. The 26 August 2026 Amendment Ordinance did not change section 7, and its official Objects and Reasons expressly reiterate the 30-day permit period. However, the current GSGSSI permit application page and 3 June 2026 fee update describe a 40-day visitor permit/fee. The 40-day wording may refer to document validity rather than permitted stay, but the Government has not explicitly explained that distinction. Do not publish a 40-day stay or treat the £250 fee as definitively tied to a 30-day stay until GSGSSI confirms the current operational permit duration and fee scope.
